title: clean can preview or delete, but cannot preview without a terminal
body:
`clean` can tell you what it would remove, or remove it, but not the first without a terminal.

## What it does today

Argument parsing accepts exactly one flag:

    --force) force=1 ;;
    *) die "clean $label: unknown argument '$arg' (only --force is accepted)"

The default path is **not** silently destructive, and that is worth stating because it is the first thing a reader assumes. Without `--force`, `clean` scans, prints all three outcome sets, and asks for confirmation. Without a tty it **refuses** -- deliberately, *"following `intent organize --force`, which refuses"* -- with the remedy *"pass --force to proceed non-interactively; it names what it removes."*

## The gap

There is no way to ask **"what would you remove?"** and get an answer without either standing at a terminal or committing to the deletion. In CI, a script, or any non-interactive context the only two reachable states are *refuse* and *delete*.

The scan is the valuable part. It already distinguishes three sets and already refuses to report a clean scan from an instrument that could not see (`lib/cmd/clean:89`). All of that work is currently gated behind a prompt.

## Why it is low

Nothing is unsafe and nothing is wrong. The refusal-without-tty is the correct default and matches the project's stated posture. This is a missing read-only mode on a command whose read-only half already exists internally.

## The comparator is in the stack already

`intent organize` previews by default and acts only under `--apply`, printing `organize: preview only -- nothing was written or removed`. `clean` inverts that: it acts by default and previews only as a side effect of asking permission. **Both are defensible; they are just different, and a reader moving between the two tools carries the wrong expectation.** Whether devbin should follow `organize` here is the actual question, and it is a convention question rather than a bug -- which puts it in the same family as issue 0035.

## Not a proposal for a flag name

`--report`, `--dry-run` and preview-by-default are three different answers with three different blast radii, and the last one changes existing behaviour for every consumer. Filed to be decided, not to be implemented as written.
